Each candidate power raises the weights to that power and fits a scale-free line to the degree distribution; the table lists the signed fit R squared and mean connectivity for powers 1 to 6, rising from -0.35 to 0.93. Power 4 is the first with R squared at least 0.8 (0.90), so it is the recommended power, highlighted in the accent color." width="100%"} For each candidate power β, raises edge weights to |w|^β and checks whether the resulting degree distribution follows a scale-free topology by fitting log(p(k)) ~ log(k). Returns the signed R² (positive when slope is negative, indicating scale-free), the slope, and the mean connectivity at each power. Recommends the lowest power achieving the R² cutoff. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [powers]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[float] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : List of candidate powers to evaluate. Defaults to `[1, 2, ..., 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20]`. [r_squared_cutoff]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.8]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Minimum signed R² to accept a power as adequate. The default is `0.8`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, return the results as a dictionary. If `False` (the default), return `self` for chaining. The result describes the whole network rather than individual nodes, so it is not written to the node table; the call is only listed by `describe()`. Use `return_dict=True` whenever you need the values. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph | dict]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A dictionary with keys `powers`, `signed_r_squared`, `slope`, `mean_connectivity`, `r_squared_cutoff`, and `recommended_power` (the lowest power achieving the cutoff, or `None`). ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~topological_overlap`) : Gene similarity from shared neighbors, the next WGCNA step. [](`~cmty_louvain`) : Find the modules of the network at the chosen power. [](`~gwas_pipeline`) : Score and rank the modules of a gene network. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Eight genes in two modules, with a co-expression weight on each edge. At power `1`, the fit of the connectivities has a rising slope, which no power law has, so its signed R² is negative. Higher powers shrink the weak weights far more than the strong ones (at power `4`, a weight of `0.8` becomes `0.41` and one of `0.2` becomes `0.0016`), and power `4` is the first to reach the cutoff of `0.8`: ::: {#49a523f3 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec import polars as pl graph = ec.Graph.from_edges( [ ("G1", "G2", 0.4), ("G1", "G3", 0.2), ("G2", "G3", 0.8), ("G2", "G4", 0.5), ("G3", "G4", 0.8), ("G4", "G5", 0.5), ("G5", "G6", 0.2), ("G5", "G7", 0.3), ("G6", "G7", 0.3), ("G6", "G8", 0.2), ("G7", "G8", 0.2), ] ) fit = graph.soft_threshold_power( powers=[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], return_dict=True ) columns = ["powers", "signed_r_squared", "slope", "mean_connectivity"] pl.DataFrame({key: fit[key] for key in columns}).with_columns( pl.all().round(2) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: {#4215c623 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} fit["recommended_power"] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 4.0 ``` ::: ::: ### Choosing the power for a co-expression network In a co-expression network, every pair of genes is linked, weighted by how closely their expression levels move together over the samples. Here the expression of 60 genes over 40 samples is simulated: three modules of 20, 15 and 10 genes each follow a shared factor, and 15 unrelated genes follow none: ::: {#f367b3d3 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np rng = np.random.default_rng(1) factors = rng.normal(size=(3, 40)) module = [0] * 20 + [1] * 15 + [2] * 10 + [-1] * 15 expression = np.array( [ (factors[m] * rng.uniform(0.6, 1.5) if m >= 0 else 0) + rng.normal(size=40) for m in module ] ) correlation = np.abs(np.corrcoef(expression)) # exactly symmetric, despite rounding correlation = (correlation + correlation.T) / 2 np.fill_diagonal(correlation, 0) coexpression = ec.from_numpy_array(correlation) fit = coexpression.soft_threshold_power(return_dict=True) columns = ["powers", "signed_r_squared", "mean_connectivity"] pl.DataFrame({key: fit[key] for key in columns}).with_columns( pl.all().round(2) ).head(8) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: The fit passes `0.8` first at power `4`, where the mean connectivity has fallen from about 11 to 0.7: ::: {#83a41ea5 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} beta = fit["recommended_power"] beta ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` 4.0 ``` ::: ::: The power is what lets the modules stand out. The many weak correlations between unrelated genes add up: at power `1`, an unrelated gene has on average 63% of the connectivity of a gene in a module, and at power `4` only 10%: ::: {#7376f92e .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} unrelated = np.array(module) == -1 def connectivity_ratio(weights): connectivity = weights.sum(axis=1) ratio = ( connectivity[unrelated].mean() / connectivity[~unrelated].mean() ) return round(float(ratio), 2) connectivity_ratio(correlation), connectivity_ratio(correlation**beta) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` (0.63, 0.1) ``` ::: ::: Drawn with the weights above `0.01` at power `4`, the three modules form tight clusters, with about 12 links per gene, while the unrelated genes, in gray, have five links at most: ::: {#6a9b2c17 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} weights = correlation**beta genes = [f"G{i}" for i in range(1, 61)] network = ec.from_numpy_array( np.where(weights > 0.01, weights, 0), node_labels=genes ) network.set_node_attrs( "module", {gene: f"M{m + 1}" for gene, m in zip(genes, module) if m >= 0}, ) network.plot(color_by="module", show_labels=False, seed=1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}
